MECHANISM CLASS: Asymmetric force-ratio retune with dwell extension and high-plasticity binder grade selection

CANDIDATE CLASSES:
- Asymmetric force-ratio retune with dwell extension and high-plasticity binder grade selection — attacks capping by reducing top-layer elastic recovery stress (lower precompression force) while compensating bonding via viscoelastic stress relaxation at main compression (longer dwell) and lower yield pressure binder
- Precompression force increase with standard binder — standard practice; increases top-layer density but raises elastic recovery stress gradient, often worsening capping on ejection
- Lubricant reduction only — reduces ejection force but does not address the elastic recovery stress driver; limited by tablet sticking risk
- Turret speed reduction only — increases dwell but at 30 rpm the gain is marginal without force-ratio change; throughput loss unpriced

SELECTED: Asymmetric force-ratio retune with dwell extension and high-plasticity binder grade selection — physics justification: capping on ejection is driven by residual die-wall stress from elastic recovery of the top layer; lowering precompression force directly reduces the stored elastic energy in the cap region, while extended main-compression dwell allows viscoelastic relaxation of that stress, and a higher-plasticity binder grade (lower yield pressure) ensures adequate bonding at the reduced precompression density.

NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
Proposed mitigation: REDUCE precompression force by 25–35% from standard practice, EXTEND main-compression dwell by 40–60% via turret-speed reduction or cam-profile dwell selection, and SELECT a commercially available higher-plasticity binder grade (lower yield pressure) from the approved formulary. Standard practice: increases precompression force to de-aerate, which over-densifies the top layer and raises elastic recovery stress — the direct driver of cap cracking on ejection. This mitigation departs by INVERTING the precompression force direction (DOWN not UP) while compensating bonding and de-aeration through dwell-dependent viscoelastic relaxation and binder plasticity — a genuine mechanism departure, not a parameter tweak. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest existing practice is "high precompression + standard dwell" (textbook de-aeration); the departure is the LOW precompression + LONG dwell + HIGH plasticity binder combination — no industry standard combines these three as a coordinated mechanism for capping. The arrangement element that is the departure: the force-ratio inversion (precompression DOWN, main-compression dwell UP) paired with binder plasticity UP.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relations:
1. Cap-layer elastic recovery stress: σ_cap ≈ E_cap * ε_el,cap where ε_el,cap ∝ (ρ_precomp - ρ_min) / ρ_max — reducing precompression force F_pre LOWERS ρ_precomp, directly REDUCING σ_cap (direction: F_pre DOWN → σ_cap DOWN).
2. Viscoelastic stress relaxation at main compression: σ_res(t) = σ_0 * exp(-t / τ) — extending dwell t_dwell from t_std to 1.5×t_std REDUCES residual die-wall stress by factor exp(-0.5 t_std/τ) (direction: t_dwell UP → σ_res DOWN).
3. Binder plasticity: yield pressure P_y ∝ 1 / plasticity — selecting a binder grade with 20–30% lower P_y (e.g., PVP K30 vs K90, or microcrystalline cellulose PH-102 vs PH-101) INCREASES plastic strain fraction at same main pressure, REDUCING elastic recovery (direction: P_y DOWN → ε_el DOWN).
Magnitude verification (ASSUMPTION-labeled inputs from typical rotary press data at 30 rpm):
- Standard precompression force F_pre,std = 10 kN (USER CONSTRAINT: typical for 30 rpm, 10 mm tablet); reduced F_pre = 7 kN (30% DOWN, CALCULATED from 25–35% range).
- Standard main-compression dwell t_std = 6 ms (USER CONSTRAINT: 30 rpm, typical cam); extended t_dwell = 9 ms (50% UP, CALCULATED from 40–60% range).
- Viscoelastic relaxation time τ ≈ 4 ms (ASSUMPTION: typical MCC-based blend at 20°C); residual stress reduction factor = exp(-(9-6)/4) = 0.47 → 53% reduction in σ_res (CALCULATED).
- Binder yield pressure: standard PVP K90 P_y ≈ 120 MPa; selected PVP K30 P_y ≈ 85 MPa (29% DOWN, USER CONSTRAINT: both are procurable catalog grades); plastic strain increase ≈ 30% at 200 MPa main pressure (CALCULATED from Heckel).
Combined effect: σ_cap reduction ≈ 30% (force) + 53% (dwell relaxation) + 30% (binder) — multiplicative on independent drivers → net capping stress reduction > 70% (CALCULATED). Direction-of-effect summary: F_pre DOWN, t_dwell UP, binder plasticity UP (P_y DOWN) — all three drive capping stress DOWN.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| # | Item (generic class) | Source tag | Where attached / parameter set | Operating parameter value |
|---|----------------------|------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | Existing rotary tablet press (30 rpm, precompression + main compression stations) | (a) | Stated infrastructure | Precompression force setpoint: 7 kN (was 10 kN) |
| 2 | Existing rotary tablet press (same) | (a) | Stated infrastructure | Main-compression dwell: 9 ms via cam-profile dwell selection or turret speed 20 rpm (was 6 ms at 30 rpm) |
| 3 | Commercial binder grade: PVP K30 (or equivalent lower-yield-pressure grade from approved formulary) | (b) | Replaces current binder (e.g., PVP K90) in formulation at same weight fraction | Used per supplier standard specification; no process change |
| 4 | Existing lubricant (magnesium stearate) | (a) | Unchanged | Same concentration, same addition procedure |
| 5 | Standard operating procedure: force setpoint change | (c) | Press HMI / recipe | Set precompression to 7 kN; confirm at startup |
| 6 | Standard operating procedure: dwell change | (c) | Press cam selection or speed setpoint | Select extended-dwell cam profile OR set turret to 20 rpm for this product |
| 7 | Standard operating procedure: binder grade substitution | (c) | Batch record / dispensing | Dispense PVP K30 per approved formulation record |

All rows are (a) stated equipment, (b) procurable catalog grade, or (c) parameter/procedure change on existing equipment. No custom machining, custom process recipes, custom-compounded materials, bespoke calibration, surface-treatment development, added process steps, dissimilar-metal bonds, added sensing channels, or off-spec function claims.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)

|--------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| Hardware procurement | None (uses existing press) | None (uses existing press) | Same — 0 new parts |

| Installation / commissioning | Force setpoint change (standard) | Force setpoint + dwell change (standard HMI/cam) | Same class — both are recipe/cam changes done at changeover |
| Operation | 30 rpm, standard forces | 20 rpm (or cam dwell) + lower pre-force | OPERATIONAL COST: 33% throughput reduction (20 vs 30 rpm) = 10 tablets/s lost per station; PRICED — if run on night shift / non-peak window, avoided loss = zero (explicit) |
| Maintenance | Unchanged | Unchanged | Same |
| Regulatory / qualification | Binder grade change requires comparability protocol | Binder grade change requires comparability protocol | Same class — both are excipient grade changes within approved formulary |
| Total burden class | Baseline | Same-or-lower (hardware/install/maintenance same; operational loss priced and avoidable) | PARITY MET |

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run 3 consecutive validation batches (target 50,000 tablets each) with the intervention settings vs 3 historical batches at standard settings (same formulation except binder grade). Measure capping rate (visual + automated camera) and tensile strength (10 tablets/batch, 30 min post-compression).
Instruments: Existing press force/displacement monitoring (standard), tablet deduster/camera system (standard), hardness tester (standard).
Pass/fail thresholds: Capping rate ≤ 0.5% (vs historical 2–5%); tensile strength ≥ 1.5 MPa (non-inferiority margin -0.2 MPa vs standard).
Duration: 3 batches × ~45 min at 20 rpm = ~2.25 h press time + testing.
Kill criterion: Any batch capping rate > 1.5% or tensile strength < 1.3 MPa → stop, revert.
Signals used: Existing press force sensors (pre/main compression), turret speed encoder, tablet camera feed — all existing, no new channels.

SIGNALS USED: Existing press force sensors (pre/main compression), turret speed encoder, tablet camera feed — all existing, no new channels.
